sep_keep_tour.accept_text: Three stops. The Lower Court, inside the gate at the south end. The Keep Hall, here at my back. And the Raven Hill Terrace, on the west side.
sep_keep_tour.description:
Commander Vane. Before we go any further - can you find the latrines?

I'm not joking and I'm not testing your sense of humour. I don't give orders to people who can't find the latrines, because an order is a place and a time, and somebody who doesn't know this keep will give me neither.

So walk it. Three stops.

The lower court, inside the gate. The Keep Hall, here at my back. And the Raven Hill Terrace, west.

That's the whole of the Sepulcher and it takes twenty minutes, and every soldier I've ever had refuse this has cost me more than twenty minutes later.

Then come back and tell me what you saw.

And don't touch anything that isn't yours.

The graveyard wing in particular. Half of what's lying about out there was laid down on purpose by somebody who's still at this keep.

sep_stone_names.accept_text: Three clusters of stones on the Raven Hill Terrace, all within a shout of me: one up the slope to the north-west, one a few paces north-east, one down to the south-west. Read the names aloud.
sep_stone_names.description:
Reader Cass. Keep your voice ordinary - I've found it carries better than whispering out here.

I read the stones in the Raven Hill wing. That's my whole office and nobody assigned it to me.

Most of them are blank.

Rain does that, over long enough. I'd accepted rain for the first year.

Then I noticed the smooth ones aren't the oldest. They're scattered - a blank stone between two legible ones cut the same season by the same mason - and rain does not choose.

Something out there rubs back.

So I'd like three clusters visited and the weeds pulled away from them, while there's still something under the weeds.

All three are on this terrace, within a shout of where I stand.

And read them aloud when you find a name.

It helps. I can't tell you how I know that and I'm certain of it.

sep_relic_shards.accept_text: Off the skeletal groundskeepers at Raven Hill Cemetery. Out of the Sepulcher's gate and north, up the hill.
sep_relic_shards.description:
Relic Hunter Darne. Don't crowd the table.

I pay for grave-goods. That's the trade, it's legal enough for this valley, and I'd rather you heard my version than Molsen's.

The skeletal groundskeepers at Raven Hill carry the best of it.

Ring-shards, buckle-bone, whatever a person was buried with - and the groundskeepers have it because they've been picking it up for years, out of the plots, and putting it in their pockets.

They're not robbing anybody. That's the part I'd want said. They're tidying, in the only way that's left to them, and they've been tidying since before the Keep had a garrison.

So what I'm doing is taking it off something that tidied it off somebody else.

I've made my peace with that. You'll make yours or you won't.

North of our gate, at Raven Hill. Intact - and don't chip them. A chipped shard is worth a quarter and tells you nothing about who it belonged to.

sep_ellowyn_sleepers.accept_text: Raven Hill Cemetery, north of the Keep once you are out of the gate. Groundskeepers and husks both.
sep_ellowyn_sleepers.description:
I count the sleepers each dusk.

Tomb-keeper. That's the post and the counting is the whole of it - I go along the chapel yard at the same hour and I count, and the number has been the same number for a long time.

Some of them have stopped lying down.

And I want to be precise about what's bothering me, because it isn't that they're up. Things get up in this valley. I've been doing this long enough.

It's where they go.

They wander off the Raven Hill plots looking for a bed. Not wandering generally - looking, going from plot to plot, and settling in one, and being moved on by whatever's already in it.

They're trying to lie down somewhere. They just can't find the right one.

So send them back where they belong.

Groundskeepers and husks both, north of the Keep, on Raven Hill.

sep_wasp_stings.accept_text: Malden's Orchard, south of the Sepulcher's gate, the other way from Raven Hill. Use tongs.
sep_wasp_stings.description:
Wrenn. Reagents. Quickly, before Darne comes over and makes it a negotiation.

The windfall wasps in Malden's Orchard are full of a venom I have been trying to buy for years.

Years. I have written to the orchard. I have gone in person, twice, and stood at the gate like a fool.

The orchard won't sell it.

And I'd understand that if they were using it - they're not. Nobody at Malden's has any interest in the wasps at all. They simply will not have anyone in among the trees, and they have never once given me a reason.

The wasps won't sell it either, which is the only part of this arrangement I can respect.

So I'd like it taken.

South of our gate, the other way from Raven Hill.

The stings are on the abdomen. Handle them with tongs - mine, if you've none, and bring them back.

sep_wreaths.accept_text: The risen farmhands of Olsen's Farthing. It is a long walk north of the Keep, past Raven Hill, where the fields begin.
sep_wreaths.description:
The Mourner. You can call me that, it's what everyone calls me and I stopped minding.

I weave wreaths out of what the dead leave behind.

Not for ceremony. There isn't a ceremony here anymore and there hasn't been since the Plague, and I'd not pretend otherwise to somebody standing in the yard looking at it.

The risen farmhands at Olsen's Farthing carry wilted sprays in their pockets.

Last year's offerings. Picked, bound, put in a coat - and never delivered, because the delivering is the part that stopped.

They're still carrying them. All of them. A field full of people walking about with flowers in their pockets for graves they were going to visit.

So I'd like them brought in.

North of the Keep, past Raven Hill, at the Farthing.

Wilted is fine. Wilted is what I work with and I've never once had anything else.

sep_gate_crows.accept_text: The Dead Field, north-east of our gate, across the Trunk Road. The harrowers, and the crows they feed.

sep_hermit_oil.accept_text: Silverpine spiders. The woods have them, and the Skittering Dark, east across the forest, has little else. Clean glands.
